results.evidence: Mountain Project lists the route at about 350 ft (106 m) with a pitch count of 23, which is the same typo-like figure as the row; a 106 m ice flow cannot have 23 pitches (about 5 m each). Searches (route name + Little Salmon River, the NB ice guide PDF from neice.com whose text is compressed/unreadable, general web) found no second source stating a pitch count, so the right value is not known. Blanking the provably false number.

Mountain Project lists 650 ft (197 m), 2 pitches, same as the row; the neighbouring UB40 is 600 ft in 3 pitches on the same page, which suggests the pitch count or length is off, but 2 pitches of ~100 m is not strictly impossible with simul-climbing or a walk between ice steps. Searched route name, area, NB ice guide PDF (unreadable compressed text) and general web: no second source. Left unchanged.

The Mountain Project route page gives headline WI5-6 M7 and its own description lists pitches P4 M7, P5 M7, P6 M7+/8, so the page itself is internally split and is the only source (the stored overview is from it). Gripped confirms only the 2001 FA by Morin and Peloquin; the FQME Charlevoix PDF and other searches (thecrag, French-language, guide blog) gave no grade. No second source, so neither the header nor the prose is changed.
